project_id: Big League Smart Contract Audit Report - QuillAudits

violation_target.vulnerability_type: Denial of Service via Liquidity Addition Failure

preconditions.description: Attacker must hold sufficient BGLG tokens to trigger the swapback threshold when transferring to the pair address
Contract must have accumulated fees in its balance exceeding the _SWAPBACK_THRESHOLD (1/10000 of totalSupply)
Contract BNB balance must be insufficient relative to token amount for liquidity addition, causing addLiquidityETH to revert

violation_target.exploit_hint: 1. Accumulate sufficient BGLG tokens in the contract through transfers to pair address (triggers fee collection). 2. Ensure contract has imbalanced BNB-to-token ratio by having tokens swapped but not enough BNB for proportional liquidity. 3. Attempt a transfer to the pair address - this will trigger _sellAndDistributeAccumulatedTKNFee() which calls addLiquidityETH. 4. The addLiquidityETH will revert due to BNB/token disparity, causing the entire transfer transaction to revert. 5. This creates a DoS condition where all transfers to the pair address fail, effectively blocking trading functionality.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a Denial of Service vulnerability in the _sellAndDistributeAccumulatedTKNFee() function. When tokens are transferred to the pair address, fees accumulate in the contract. Once the contract's token balance exceeds the swapback threshold (1/10000 of totalSupply), the function attempts to swap tokens for BNB and then add liquidity. However, with fees.liquidity = 0, TKNtoLiquidity becomes 0, but BNBtoLiquidity > 0 from the swap. Calling addLiquidityETH with BNB but 0 tokens causes the router to revert, making all transfers to the pair fail.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Inject sufficient BGLG tokens into the contract to exceed the swapback threshold. 2. Trigger a transfer to the pair address which calls _sellAndDistributeAccumulatedTKNFee(). 3. The function will swap tokens for BNB, then attempt addLiquidityETH with BNB but 0 tokens (since liquidity fee is 0). 4. This causes the transaction to revert, demonstrating the DoS condition. 5. Verify the contract remains unpaused (the oracle check).
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Set up token contract interface and get pair address. 2. Use deal() to inject tokens into the contract balance (not attacker). 3. Transfer tokens from attacker to pair to trigger fee collection and swapback. 4. The addLiquidityETH will revert due to token/BNB imbalance. 5. Assert that paused == false to pass the oracle.
